youtube_title: Lake Station, Indiana: murdered in his own doorway, 1888 (Lake Station request)
youtube:
You asked for Lake Station! On a Sunday evening in September 1888, while a Michigan Central freight train switched cars in front of his house west of Lake Station, 72-year-old George Wolf was shot and killed in his own doorway. The trainmen heard two shots. No weapon was found, the paper said it couldn't have been robbery, and the coroner's verdict was murder, "probably caused by tramps." The Chesterton Tribune called it "shrouded in mystery," and when his widow died the next spring, it still called it a mysterious murder. facebook:
You asked for Lake Station!
Two shots, a stone's throw from help. That's how the Chesterton Tribune told it in September 1888.
George Wolf was 72, feeble, partly deaf, and home alone that Sunday evening, at his house west of Lake Station, about 250 feet north of the tracks. His wife was away in Hegewisch caring for a granddaughter.
About 7:30, a Michigan Central freight train was switching cars in front of his house. The trainmen heard two shots. Railroad men went to the house. He had been murdered in his own doorway.
No weapon was found, and the paper said it couldn't have been robbery. The coroner's verdict: murder, "probably caused by tramps."
The paper called it "shrouded in mystery." When his widow died the next spring, it still called it a mysterious murder.
LaPorte After Dark. More LaPorte County history: laporteweathernow.com/history
